item.title: Everything we’re excited for at London Fashion Week AW26 - BRICKS Magazine
item.description: London Fashion Week returns with a line-up that moves from postal theatrics to sculptural dioramas, from Milanese cherubs to Yemeni souks. Below, see the runways, presentations, and immersive installations we’re most excited about. Maximilian Raynor is posting one last kiss Homegrown favourite Maximilian Raynor is returning with another camp runway collection, this time entitled Post Me One Last Kiss. item.title: Ella Douglas puts the pedal down for AW26 - BRICKS Magazine
item.description: The Oxford-born, London-based designer’s latest capsule collection spotlights truck drivers, tyre-track leather and mop-made gowns.

item.title: Chet Lo’s Night Market reimagines the runway as a space of access and community - BRICKS Magazine
item.description: In partnership with Hair & Care and community platform Red Flagged, the Asian-American designer staged his AW26 collection as an accessible runway experience, expanding his tactile knitwear world to blind and low vision guests and the Asian creative diaspora.

item.title: The collections we can’t stop thinking about from London Fashion Week AW26 - BRICKS Magazine
item.description: Across immersive installations, performance-led presentations, graduate breakthroughs and highly covetable collaborations, London Fashion Week AW26 showed that its strength lies in variety.

item.title: Saint Harison traces heartbreak, forgiveness and growth on ghosted - BRICKS Magazine
